facts.fact: UNDP Malawi reports that Mwanza District Council uses LORMIS to issue electronic tickets for market fees, vehicle parking and border entry fees and has a business registration component; the story says the system tracks who has paid and who has not, but does not describe a register of payers with bills against them.

UNDP Malawi describes LORMIS as a system built and run by the Mwanza District Council's own systems analyst, working on an Android application and a second platform, with supervisors at the council office tracing transactions; it states no reporting to a national system.
UNDP Malawi states that Mwanza is using all components of LORMIS; its developer hopes more districts will adopt it, and no other council or total of councils is given.
UNDP Malawi states that Mwanza adopted LORMIS with the support of the United Nations Development Programme; the developer is the council's own systems analyst and no ministry owner is named.

systems.platform: Android application plus a second platform; homegrown
systems.owner: Mwanza District Council, with UNDP support
systems.tiers: Mwanza District Council: market and parking tickets, border entry fees, business registration
